newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- recovering from losses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- recovering from losses.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds fell about 1/4 point in early trading after new economic data on inflation and employment were released, but prices retraced their steps later in the morning, traders said.

"It's a little hesitant here," one trader said, before the Philadelphia Fed figures were released at 1000 EDT. Those figures helped the fixed income markets recover some of their early losses, but munis are typically slowest to catch the ride.

The Philadelphia Fed said its business activity index was 1.6 in May, versus 5.7 in April. The government long bond recovered from an early drop, with the long bond down 1/32 at 96-22/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
Earlier data viewed negatively by the market included the Labor Department's release of initial claims, which fell to 319,000 the week of May 10.

And the Labor Department also said the consumer price index for April rose 0.1 percent, and increased 0.3 percent at the core. The figure was almost in line with economists' expectations, which pegged the overall figure at up 0.1 percent and o.2 percent higher at the core.

The Federal Reserve's industrial production figure April, which was unchanged from March and below the expectations of a 0.2 percent rise. Capacity utilization was 83.4 percent, compared to expectations for 84.1 percent.

In debt futures, the June municipal contract moved back into positive territory after the Philadelphia Fed figure. It was up 4/32 at 116-6/32, while June T-bonds were unchanged at 110-5/32. The MOB spread widened to 193 ticks, compared to 189 at the close on Wednesday.
Municipal bond sales for Thursday are expected to total $371 million in 23 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $274 million in 12 sales, with a $79 million Lorain County, Ohio, variable rate bond deal through Bear, Stearns & Co. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 11 sales totaling $97 million are on the schedule. A $60 million Montgomery County, Pa., issue at 1030 EDT is the largest.
